stories.title: Families often dictate psychiatric care in low-income regions
stories.summary: A scoping review of 36 studies across Africa, Asia and the Middle East found that family members predominantly shape psychiatric care decisions. The research, published in PLOS Mental Health, identified little evidence of shared decision-making, noting that family dominance often overrides the preferences of service users themselves.

stories.title: Relationships and communication drive mental health implementation
stories.summary: Researchers studying the Mental Health Implementation Network in England found that relationships, communication and time were the primary factors in adopting evidence-based interventions. The study, published in BMC Psychiatry, suggests these human elements were essential for bridging the gap between mental health research and clinical practice.

stories.title: Kentucky lawmakers renew push for juvenile mental health facility
stories.summary: Kentucky lawmakers are seeking funding for a specialized juvenile mental health facility following reports of an autistic teenager held in a flooded cell for 20 hours. Advocates state the incident highlights ongoing systemic failures within the state’s juvenile detention centers. The facility remains a proposed solution.

stories.title: Madison conference to address mental health for youth of color
stories.summary: The BIPOC Mental Health Coalition of Dane County is hosting a conference on November 7 to discuss mental health challenges facing Black, Indigenous and other youth of color. The event will feature youth-led panels and present report findings on access to care and community support resources.

stories.title: Psychodrama training offered for trauma and addiction clinicians
stories.summary: A February 2027 workshop titled Introduction to Psychodrama will train clinicians in action-based therapy. The program claims to help clients step onto a stage to re-author their internal stories. The session costs 180 dollars and provides 6 continuing education units for participating mental health professionals.

stories.title: Acne-induced dyspigmentation linked to mental health struggles
stories.summary: A study in the Archives of Dermatological Research found that acne-induced macular dyspigmentation negatively affects mental health and social functioning. Participants reported that these marks were often more difficult to treat than the acne itself, leading to significant frustration for individuals with darker skin types.

stories.summary: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott has praised the team’s Huddle 94 program, which facilitates small group discussions on life stressors. Prescott noted the resource aims to create supportive conversations among players, suggesting such initiatives might have provided necessary help for former teammate Marshawn Kneeland before his death.

stories.title: Suicide at federal mental health agency prompts workforce grief
stories.summary: A suicide within the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration has caused renewed distress among the HHS workforce. The agency, which manages national mental health initiatives, has faced multiple traumatic workplace incidents. Help is available via the 988 suicide and crisis lifeline in the United States.

stories.summary: Kintegra Health opened a pediatric behavioral health center in Gastonia this October to address the mental and emotional needs of children. The facility arrives as the county continues to manage rising rates of opioid addiction and overdoses, offering specialized support for local youth and adolescents.

stories.title: Meditation study finds no advantage over muscle relaxation
stories.summary: A randomized controlled trial published in PLOS One found that four weeks of loving-kindness meditation did not outperform muscle relaxation exercises in reducing pain or improving social well-being. Participants practicing muscle relaxation actually reported higher perceived social support, though neither method proved superior for pain management.

The organization states that demand for its support program exceeds capacity, with over 200 applications received for 17 available spots. The sessions are intended to assist veterans and their families with trauma recovery.

stories.summary: Researchers at New York University and the University of Delaware found that earlier bedtimes were associated with greater weight loss among adults with prediabetes. The study, published in Nursing Research, suggests that sleep timing may be a lifestyle factor to assist with weight management.

stories.summary: Major professional societies recommend cognitive behavioral therapy as the first-line treatment for chronic insomnia. The therapy focuses on correcting sleep misconceptions and improving habits without the use of medication.

stories.title: Resistance band exercises for mobility
stories.summary: Strength coach Matt Van Mol suggests a four-move resistance band routine to address seized shoulders, hips and lower back. He claims the movements improve mobility by increasing the range one can actually control. The routine requires a long-loop band and four minutes of daily effort.

stories.title: Four-ingredient millet pancakes
stories.summary: These millet pancakes require only millet flour, a ripe banana, milk and baking powder. The recipe takes 20 minutes and relies on the banana to sweeten and bind the batter. The author notes that lumps should be avoided, as they leave uneven pockets in the finished pancakes.

stories.title: Oatly expands into fibre drinks
stories.summary: Oatly is launching a fibre drink range, citing consumer interest in gut health. The products contain 5 to 6 grams of fibre per 250ml serving. Global president Daniel Ordonez described the launch as a natural extension of the company's existing portfolio, built on 30 years of research.

stories.title: Nutrition literacy linked to adolescent eating habits
stories.summary: A study of 494 adolescents in Ghana found a positive association between nutrition literacy and eating behaviour. General health literacy and parental socio-economic status showed no significant link to how the students ate. The study used Pearson correlation and multiple linear regression analysis to reach its findings.

stories.title: Japanese 4D Microbiome Project
stories.summary: The Japanese 4D Microbiome Project is a multicenter study examining the gut microbiome's association with health and disease. Initiated in 2015, the project involves collaboration from hospitals and research institutes. Participants provide written informed consent and are not compensated financially for their involvement in the data collection.

stories.title: Study finds arsenic in rice-based cereals
stories.summary: A Clean Label report found that some rice-based cereals contain nearly 12 times the arsenic found in cereals made from other grains. Study officials suggested that the category still has work to do to deliver the nutrient density found in simple, minimally processed alternatives like eggs.

stories.title: Enzymatic pathway converts dairy byproduct to sugar
stories.summary: Researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences have developed a coenzyme-free pathway to produce galacto-N-biose from lactose. This sugar building block is found in the gut's protective mucus layer. The process converts a low-value byproduct of the dairy industry into a functional disaccharide.

stories.title: Plant-based milk and nutrient intake
stories.summary: A study published in the Lancet Planetary Health suggests that switching from dairy to plant-based milk alternatives could carry health risks due to lower levels of vital vitamins and minerals. The research compares the nutritional value of various dairy and plant-based products found in supermarkets.

stories.title: Clinical review supports kefir consumption
stories.summary: A review of more than two dozen clinical trials concludes that kefir offers small improvements to the gut, cardiovascular system and mouth lining. Scientists suggest the fermented drink may live up to its reputation as a microbiome powerhouse, despite its potentially accidental origin centuries ago.

stories.title: Study links plant-based milk swaps to nutrient gaps
stories.summary: Experts writing in the Lancet Planetary Health journal suggest that swapping dairy for plant-based alternatives like oat or almond milk could lead to vitamin and mineral deficiencies. The study notes that children, teenagers and women appear to be the most affected by these dietary changes.

stories.title: Decoding fruit juice labels
stories.summary: Consumers often assume products labelled as fruit juice or fruit-based drinks offer identical nutritional benefits. Dr Eileen Canday notes that these products differ significantly in fruit content and sugar composition. Understanding labels is presented as an essential step for shoppers before making a purchase.

stories.title: Gut bacteria genetic profiles and ageing
stories.summary: A study published in Nature investigated the link between gut microbial single-nucleotide variants and human health phenotypes. Researchers suggest that hidden genetic differences among gut bacteria may hold clues to metabolism and ageing, even when two people possess similar types of gut bacteria.

stories.title: Nanoparticles target senescent cells in cancer
stories.summary: Researchers have developed a nanoparticle treatment in mice to eliminate senescent cells that drive tissue scarring. The approach aims to make tumors more sensitive to immune-boosting therapies. The study suggests this method might one day be applied to humans to help treat cancer-linked fibrosis.

stories.title: Data architecture in longevity trials
stories.summary: Designerly's Cooper Adwin argues that secure data architecture is critical for decentralized longevity trials. Tracking biomarker endpoints across jurisdictions requires sustained access to historical measurements. The author suggests that infrastructure gaps currently undermine the ability of founders to translate development capital into interpretable evidence.

stories.title: AgeReverse launches direct-to-consumer store
stories.summary: Canadian longevity company AgeReverse has launched an online store for U.S. consumers. The company says the move provides direct access to its science-driven products and educational information. This expansion complements its existing retail presence on platforms like Amazon.

stories.summary: Researchers from three Chinese universities are studying how electroacupuncture affects gene and protein signals in rats with chronic atrophic gastritis. research.title: Scientists discover mysterious “lonely” brain waves linked to memory loss
research.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising link between Alzheimer’s-related protein buildup, disrupted brain waves during deep sleep, and fading memory. The findings suggest that hidden changes in how the brain processes memories overnight may contribute to age-related memory loss long before Alzheimer’s symptoms appear.
